summary: It is an interactive Earth-change dashboard that provides a demonstration tool to help visualize flood and fire dynamics using a map-based, time-based interface. It makes complex radar-style environmental change easier to understand for broad audiences and highlights why monitoring land and water changes matters for ecosystems, agriculture, and communities.
details:
It is an interactive dashboard for exploring how Earth’s surface changes over time. Regions in Japan and Brazil serve as demo walkthroughs for flood and fire scenarios, shown using an atlas, timelines, playback, and comparison tools. It helps users understand complex environmental changes and their potential effects on ecosystems, agriculture, infrastructure, and communities.

The app is built with JavaScript, React, and Vite, with Three.js/React Three Fiber supporting 3D visualization. It runs in a web browser; no specialized hardware is required. The project also includes ASF and Earthdata source references and catalog workflows. However, the current demo event layers are synthetic illustrations, not measured NISAR observations. The main focus on the design was to keep demonstrations clear, concise and engaging while avoiding confusion between simulations and real satellite data, while also serving as a useful tool for analysis on the constantly shifting form of Earth. The approach was to turn the data from Earth's constantly changing surface and structure into an interactive, time-based visualization, with the intention of making radar remote-sensing concepts more accessible and encouraging future integration of validated NISAR data.
